=== c1-tenant
- SEC-H1: partial | before=yes after=yes
   residual: In production no path files work under 'dev' any more. But the reservation the lane notes describe ("no user can create or rename a tenant to dev") is false: any tenant owner/admin can take the slug through main's 'owners update tenants' RLS policy by nulling created_by in the same UPDATE. Wherever QCOMPASS_ENV=dev runs against a DB that real users share, the original capture still works. The 20261031200400 backfill (new finding) also hands legacy agent rows to such a tenant. Runs filed under 'dev' before the fix are never reassigned. The documented NOT VALID remediation (rename, then validate) leaves the squatter as a member of that tenant id, so they keep those rows.
- REV-B1: closed | before=yes after=yes
   residual: The API process has no real pricing caller, so the budget-hook part is shown only by a synthetic route in the test. _run_coroutine blocks the event loop thread while cancel_run runs (see newFindings).
- SEC-verify-resolve_tenant: closed | before=no after=yes
   residual: The fix is correct. The repository's regression test for it never ran the nondeterministic query on BEFORE: it errors before reaching it. The slug guard's regex is also narrower than claimed (see newFindings), though resolve_tenant only takes the id branch for canonical 8-4-4-4-12 input, so no shadowing comes of it today.
- SEC-H1-slug-migration-20261031200000: partial | before=yes after=no
   residual: The NOT VALID state also makes every later UPDATE of the violating tenant row fail (for example subscription_tier changes) until the slug is changed. The remediation in W1-platform.md:261 does not handle the agent-row backfill that runs right after.

  NEW [NIT/confirmed] supabase/migrations/20261031200000_qcompass_tenant_slug_guard.sql:28 The UUID-shape regex does not cover every form Postgres casts to uuid, so the lane notes' claim 'refuses a slug shaped like any UUID form Postgres casts' is false.
     scenario: Postgres accepts a hyphen after any group of four hex digits. Slug 'a0ee-bc99-9c0b-4ef8-bb6d-6bb9-bd38-0a11' passes the CHECK and `::uuid` casts it to a0eebc99-9c0b-4ef8-bb6d-6bb9bd380a11 (confirmed on AFTER by scratch-c1/test_c1_resolve.py::test_slug_guard_misses_a_castable_uuid_form). It cannot be exploited today, because AuthStore.resolve_tenant only takes the id branch for canonical 8-4-4-4-12 input. Any future lookup that casts non-canonical input would reopen the shadowing.
     fix: Check castability instead of a regex: `slug !~* '^[{]?[0-9a-f-]{32,39}[}]?$'` combined with a strip-hyphens length-32 test, or a check helper function that tries `slug::uuid` and returns false on an exception.

   residual: The direct job-insert vector is closed. The plan-limit bypass part of H2's impact is still open through another table: the tenant owner or admin can rewrite tenants.subscription_tier, which plans.enforce_at_enqueue trusts (see new finding). Nothing detects or reports jobs, run_results or run-artifacts that forged jobs wrote before the fix: no NOTICE or audit query for jobs where tenant_id <> runs.tenant_id. Victim run_results that a forged job upserted before the fix stay in place and are served by the tenant-joined result query. test_h2_run_reads_ignore_rows_written_under_another_tenant cannot run on BEFORE, so its fail-before is a TypeError.

Use tenant_role in ('owner','admin','member'), or require tenant_id is null, since no client writes tenant runs. Report existing runs where the author is not a member of tenant_id.

=== c3-queue
- SF1: closed | before=yes after=yes
   residual: (1) The terminal event is written only when the janitor changed the run (`if found`). A run that is already terminal but has no terminal event stays without one, so its streams end only through the idle bound. Example: the worker died between set_run_status('completed') at worker.py:180 and the status emit at :185. (2) StreamBound.expired() is checked only on polls that return no events, so the 7200 s cap is not enforced while events keep arriving. (3) The default idle bound (900 s) is shorter than the job timeout (3600 s), which can abort healthy streams (new finding). (4) The new dead-letter UPDATE on runs introduces a lock-order deadlock with cancel_run (new finding).
- SF2: closed | before=yes after=yes
   residual: (1) The lease identity is the worker_id alone. An abandoned handler thread and the worker's own _fail share that id, and _fail holds the lease until complete(). An in-flight write from the abandoned thread can therefore land after _fail. Also, set_run_status protects only 'canceled', so a run can go from failed to completed, or from completed to running when a job is re-run after complete() failed (new finding, repro). (2) The lease checks in emit and save_result are plain EXISTS reads with no row lock. A worker event can get a job_events id above the cancel's 'status: canceled' event; this is cosmetic because streams stop at the first terminal event. (3) _GuardedQueue passes complete, heartbeat, cancel_run, enqueue_run, _emit and engine through unguarded (worker.py:76-79).
- L3: partial | before=yes after=yes
   residual: The caps are trivially bypassed: the '^' operator, and constants wrapped in an allowed call, both get past _constant_digits. The sympy work these bypasses trigger holds the GIL, so the thread-based timeout cannot interrupt them and the heartbeat starves. A malicious custom potential still wedges each worker that claims it until liveness kills that worker (about 90 s), for up to max_attempts workers. Non-finite or very large timeout values break every job. The worker keeps claiming jobs after an abandonment. See the new findings.
  NEW [MEDIUM/confirmed] backend/src/ucgle_f1/m2_scalar/potentials.py:132 The custom-potential caps (SEC-L3) can be bypassed. The AST check treats '^' as BitXor, but sympify(convert_xor=True) turns it into '**'. _constant_digits also returns None for any subtree that contains a Call, so constants wrapped in Rational() or sqrt() escape both the exponent check and the digit check.
     scenario: An authenticated tenant with run scope submits potential.kind='custom' with customPython 'phi^(9^9^9)', or 'phi**(Rational(9)**Rational(9)**Rational(9))', 'phi**(sqrt(81)**sqrt(81)**sqrt(81))', '(((((Rational(9)**64)**64)**64)**64)**64)'. _check_custom_size accepts each one, and sympify then computes 9**387420489 or 9**(64**5). Repro scratch-c3/expr_bypass.py: all four hang past 15 s on AFTER, while the original phi**(9**9**9) is rejected in 0.00 s. validate_config (tools/simulator.py:121) only 
     fix: Do not let sympify parse the raw string. Either build the sympy expression yourself from the validated AST and check magnitudes at each Pow when both operands are numbers (or use sympify(convert_xor=False) plus parse_expr(evaluate=False) and inspect the unevaluated tree before calling doit()), or re
  NEW [MEDIUM/confirmed] backend/src/ucgle_f1/worker.py:448 The thread-based JOB_TIMEOUT cannot interrupt a handler that holds the GIL inside one long C call, such as the sympy/CPython big-integer pow that L3 cited. runner.join(timeout) never returns on time, the heartbeat thread starves, and /healthz cannot answer.
     scenario: Repro scratch-c3/gil_worker.py: Worker(job_timeout_seconds=0.5, lease 1 s, heartbeat 0.2 s) running a handler that compiles 'phi^(9^9^7)'. The handler starts at 1.06 s and ends at 3.58 s. The one heartbeat and the join both happen at 3.58 s. No JOB_TIMEOUT, and complete() records the job as succeeded. With the 9^9^9 payload the pow runs for hours, so the lease lapses. The janitor on another worker requeues the job to the next worker, which wedges too. Liveness (3x30 s) restarts each one, and thi
     fix: Run handlers, or at least compile_potential and other user-controlled symbolic work, in a child process that the loop can kill on timeout (multiprocessing/ProcessPool with terminate, or setrlimit RLIMIT_CPU in the child). Keep the heartbeat and health server in the parent.
  NEW [LOW/confirmed] backend/src/ucgle_f1/worker.py:51 job_timeout_seconds_default accepts inf and any value above threading.TIMEOUT_MAX (e.g. 1e10), and runner.join() then raises OverflowError. The handler thread is left running unabandoned with `lost` unset, complete() is never called, and every job dead-letters. The CLI --job-timeout-seconds is not validated at all: -1 makes every job time out instantly.

The finally block stops the heartbeat, the lease expires and the janitor requeues the job.      fix: Require math.isfinite(value) and 0 < value <= threading.TIMEOUT_MAX (or clamp) in the env parser and also in Worker.__init__ for the CLI/constructor value. Treat any exception from join as an abandonment: set lost, append the thread to abandoned, and call _fail.
  NEW [LOW/confirmed] supabase/migrations/20261031200300_qcompass_queue_lease_guard.sql:49 New lock-order inversion. The dead-letter branch locks the jobs row (FOR UPDATE in the loop) and then updates the runs row, while JobQueue.cancel_run (jobs.py:335-356) locks the runs row FOR UPDATE and then updates jobs. A cancel that races a dead-letter of the same run deadlocks.
     scenario: Repro scratch-c3/db_repro.py, which emulates cancel_run statement by statement: connection C runs `select ... from runs where id='r_dl' for update`, then reap_expired_jobs() runs on another connection, then C runs the jobs update. AFTER gives `{'reap': 'DeadlockDetected', 'cancel': 'committed'}`; BEFORE gives `{'reap': 1, 'cancel': 'committed'}`. reap handles every expired job in one transaction, so the victim rolls back the whole janitor pass (Worker.run_once raises and logs 'worker loop error'
     fix: Use one lock order. In cancel_run, lock the run's jobs first (`select id from jobs where run_id=:id for update`) and then the run. Alternatively, in reap, take the run row with `for update skip locked` (or nowait) and leave that job for the next pass when the run is locked.

     scenario: Repro scratch-c3/inflight_repro.py, with delays standing in for DB latency (0.7 s on the handler's UPDATE, 0.5 s on _fail's complete): the handler calls set_run_status('completed') just before the 0.5 s timeout. Final state: run 'completed', job 'failed' with JOB_TIMEOUT, status events [queued, failed], and no result stored. The same predicate lets a re-run of a requeued job flip a completed run back to 'running'. That happens when complete() raised after the handler had already set the run comp
     fix: Make terminal run states sticky in SQL for lease-carrying writes (`status not in ('completed','failed','canceled')`, allowing only running to terminal).   NEW [LOW/plausible] backend/src/ucgle_f1/m8_agent/settings.py:73 Healthy runs are aborted by the stream bound.      fix: Guard self.abandoned with a lock, or filter in place under the lock (or only on the loop thread).

- SF4: partial | before=yes after=yes
   residual: The backfill hands all legacy agent memory to slug 'dev' without checking created_by IS NULL. Approval-token ids leak through agent_tool_calls.requestJson, which members can read. Approval tokens can be replayed: '*' tokens for any TTL, and one-shot tokens across instances. Verification: the copied test_sf4_agent_memory_is_tenant_scoped fails on 3d2355a at line 728 (stolen token 200 != 403), which is the bug's own reason, and passes on 040bc36. test_sf4_agent_tenancy_migration_is_reversible fails on 3d2355a only with a TypeError (tenant kwarg); it guards reversibility and is not a bug detector.
- L2: open | before=no after=yes
   residual: Not fixed. The cross-tenant existence oracle (taken somewhere, and not mine means foreign) is unchanged through the API, and also works through a PostgREST runs insert that needs no tenant membership. Cross-tenant id squatting also works (new finding). The regression test checks only wording.

In the same deploy, 200400 runs `select id into dev from tenants where slug='dev'` and `update ... set tenant_id = dev where tenant_id is null`.      fix: Backfill only to `slug='dev' and created_by is null`, or better, leave legacy rows NULL (their real tenant is unknown). Fix the migration comment, which says the rows were written by the dev path.
  NEW [LOW/confirmed] backend/src/ucgle_f1/m8_agent/memory/store.py:211 consume_approval reads the token, checks it, then writes consumed=true, guarded only by a per-process threading.RLock. A one-shot token can be spent twice by concurrent requests on different API instances.
     scenario: deploy/qcompass-api.yaml:28 sets maxScale 10. Two POST /api/runs (or cancel_run) requests with the same start_run token hit two instances. Both sessions s.get the row with consumed=False, both UPDATE by primary key with no condition, and both return True. Repro on both trees (two ConversationStore instances with separate locks and a barrier after the read): 'one-shot token accepted 2 times'. Pre-existing; the fix did not address it.
     fix: Spend the token atomically: `update agent_approval_tokens set consumed=true where "tokenId"=:t and tenant_id=:tenant and not consumed and ("expiresAt" is null or "expiresAt" > now()) returning scopes`, or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE.
  NEW [LOW/confirmed] backend/src/ucgle_f1/m8_agent/server.py:300 /v1/chat stores raw tool arguments, approval_token included, in agent_tool_calls.requestJson. The new 'tenant members read agent tool calls' policy exposes those bearer secrets to every member, viewers included, contradicting the migration's 'approval tokens stay service-only'.
     scenario: An acme run-scope caller chats, and the model calls cancel_run with {run_id:'nope', approval_token:tok}. cancel_run returns NOT_FOUND before spending the token. A viewer added to acme then runs `select "requestJson" from agent_tool_calls` via PostgREST and sees the token id, while `select count(*) from agent_approval_tokens` = 0. The token still verifies (consume_approval returned True afterwards). Using it needs run scope in acme, so the impact is limited, but the stated invariant is broken.
     fix: Redact approval_token, and any *_token argument, before record_tool_call, or exclude requestJson from the member policy (a view or column privileges).
  NEW [LOW/confirmed] backend/src/ucgle_f1/m8_agent/memory/store.py:190 Approval tokens with scope '*' are never consumed and accept any required scope, and the TTL is caller-chosen with no upper bound. A very large TTL raises an unhandled ValueError (500).
     scenario: POST /api/approvals {scopes:['*'], ttl_seconds:1e9} succeeds (about 31 years). The token then approves start_run, cancel_run, start_run, scan_parameters, all True, on both trees. It outlives revocation of the API key or membership that minted it. ttl_seconds=1e13 gives 'ValueError: year 318914 is out of range' (500).
     fix: Cap ttl_seconds (e.g. at most 3600) and reject non-positive values with 422. Drop '*' or make it single-use, and bind tokens to the issuing principal.
  NEW [LOW/confirmed] backend/src/ucgle_f1/m8_agent/qcompass_routes.py:296 Run ids are one global namespace that clients choose, so any tenant, or any signed-up user via PostgREST, can squat ids another tenant will submit and make that tenant's submits fail with 409.
     scenario: acme POSTs runId 'kawai-kim-natural', then globex's POST with the same runId gets 409. Separately, eve (an authenticated user with no tenant) inserts public.runs(id='acme-next-run', author_user_id=eve, tenant_id null), which 20261031200200:13-18 allows. acme's later POST with runId 'acme-next-run' gets 409. Both confirmed on AFTER.
     fix: Stop using client runIds as the primary key: generate ids server-side and keep the client value as a per-tenant alias with a unique (tenant_id, alias) index.
  NEW [NIT/plausible] backend/src/ucgle_f1/m8_agent/memory/store.py:172 agent_plans.path is an absolute server filesystem path under agent-sandbox/<conversation_id>/, not namespaced by tenant and built from an unsanitised conversation_id. The new member-read policy exposes this path, the same class of leak SEC-L4 removed from provenanceSidecar.
     scenario: save_plan is not currently reachable over HTTP (mcp_server._dispatch has no save_plan), so this matters only once it is wired up. Then a conversation_id like '../../x' would write outside the sandbox, two tenants sharing a conversation_id would share a directory, and members would read the absolute host path.
     fix: Use safe_join/safe_component with a tenant root, as qcompass_routes._tenant_root does, and store a relative logical reference.
  NEW [NIT/confirmed] backend/src/ucgle_f1/m8_agent/tools/simulator.py:137 start_run spends the approval token before the A6 and config checks, and links the run to a hypothesisId it never checks. get_hypothesis has no production caller, so a run can cite a nonexistent or foreign tenant's hypothesis.
     scenario: POST /api/runs with a valid one-shot token but no cfg.agent returns AUDIT_VIOLATION, and the token is already consumed. A globex run can carry hypothesisId 'hyp_<acme id>'. This leaks nothing, since the link is filed under globex, but A6 traceability is not enforced.
     fix: Validate cfg.agent first, check get_hypothesis(hypothesisId, tenant=tenant) is not None, then consume the token, as cancel_run already orders it.

 "wireShape": "The boundary is in the backend request model, not the frontend service layer. The API carries potential parameters in the units the Configurator shows. The one table of names and units is ucgle_f1.domain.POTENTIAL_PARAM_FORMS, and every name has exactly one unit:\n- starobinsky: M [M_Pl].\n- natural: f [GeV] and Lambda4 [M_Pl^4] (the Configurator's names), or f_a and Lambda [M_Pl] (M2's names). M2's names are kept because Decision 11 put them in kawai-kim-natural.json, and R4 protects the adapter round-trip test and the audit configs that use them. A dict that mixes the two is refused with 422 \"ambiguous\".\n- hilltop: V0 [M_Pl^4], mu [GeV], p (integer 2 to 64, default 4).\n- any kind: optional phi0 [M_Pl]. custom: the snippet's own symbols.\n\nThe one conversion is Potential.engine(), using the existing M_PL_GEV (no second constant): f_a = f/M_PL_GEV, Lambda = Lambda4**0.25, mu = mu/M_PL_GEV. Everything else passes through as the same float objects. It returns an EnginePotential, so nothing is converted twice. RunPipeline applies it at the M2 step, beside the physics lane's Gamma_phi conversion.\n\nA RunConfig is stored and echoed exactly as the client sent it. CosmologyPotential (the run route's model) now subclasses domain.Potential and also requires every parameter of the chosen form. POST /api/qcompass/domains/{d}/runs calls the plugin's validate_problem before queueing; a failure is 422 INVALID_INPUT with a message naming each problem.
